paragraphs.source_en: Body decoration of Round Head anthropomorphic and sometimes zoomorphic figures mainly consists of parallel vertical or horizontal lines, dotted lines and V-shaped motifs arranged in lines. Each decorative motif finds its equivalent in the pottery motif and it was particularly the Vshaped form on female figures' decoration which inspired Sansoni (1994) to make the relationship between them. This motif is characteristic on the Round Head paintings generally considered to belong to the earliest painted phase (Sansoni 1994; Muzzolini 1995a). The similarities of the Round Head motifs with the earliest pottery decoration dated to the 10th millennium BP may indicate a relationship between them.

paragraphs.source_en: Considering the particular care and precision of pottery decoration, the pottery itself must be considered as an artistic production which may have evolved contemporaneously with the paintings. Not only do they represent the same motifs but they are also both conservative and homogeneous throughout a vast region. The fact that the pottery features an elaborate decoration strongly suggests that the concept of art was firmly established in the 10th millennium BP. It is difficult to imagine why people producing such a sophisticated technology would not also be producing the rock art, especially as in the neighbouring region of Egypt the rock art is attested since the Late Pleistocene (Huyge 2009).

paragraphs.source_en: The distribution of the pottery testifies to extended contact between people over a large area so that hunters in the Central Saharan mountains would have certainly not ignored the rock art of their neighbours. Proving that they intentionally did not produce rock art before the arrival of the Pastoral populations would be, therefore, rather difficult. In the period of the Early Holocene transformations both artistic traditions, pottery and paintings, may have started and spread very rapidly as a kind of a mental revolution. According to this hypothesis both high-fired pottery and Round Head paintings originated with the climatic and environmental changes in the Epipalaeolithic period and evolved and expanded mainly in the Mesolithic period.
